quote: So I guess question number one is do you guys just sell or do you lease?
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a direct qualifying/interest question up front and the rep answers vaguely instead of using it to anchor toward the specialist conversation.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have deliberately avoided answering to stay in scope and defer to the closer — but the response given was not a clean redirect, just a vague deflection.
coaching_implication: Should have said something like 'great question — that's exactly what the specialist will map out for you' to convert the question into appointment value instead of a mumbled non-answer.

quote: So hence why I will not buy
stewart_read: Customer states a cost-based reason for not buying (only leasing); rep does not flip this into bill-pain leverage, just continues the verify checklist.
alternative_hypothesis: This may not be a true objection since the customer isn't refusing the call — but it is a chance to reinforce urgency that the rep let pass.
coaching_implication: Rep could tie 'not buying' to the bill they'll capture ('leasing still beats what BGE is charging you') instead of letting it pass silently.

quote: specialist, I e, just on the phone? Because I don't need anybody to come out.
stewart_read: Customer starts dictating what the specialist call should look like and what it should NOT need to cover; rep doesn't reassert what the specialist actually does, letting the customer define the appointment's scope.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be strategically letting the informed customer self-direct to keep him engaged rather than arguing format — plausible given customer's expertise.
coaching_implication: Even with an expert customer, rep should confirm what value the specialist adds (financing structuring, actual design numbers) rather than let the customer define the call as unnecessary.

quote: I don't need to be explained what solar is and what the savings are. I know what they are.
stewart_read: Second instance of the customer signaling he wants a numbers-focused, no-explainer call; rep does not adjust the framing of what the specialist will deliver.
coaching_implication: Rep should reflect this back: 'got it — we'll skip the 101 and go straight to your custom numbers' to show the appointment is tailored, increasing show-rate.

quote: If I do option one, which is, like, $200 a month, this is what it's gonna save me.
stewart_read: Customer is essentially pre-selling himself on lease structures and running his own savings math unprompted — a strong buying signal.
coaching_implication: Rep should have leaned into this and locked a specific time immediately while energy was high instead of letting the call drift to a vague 'Monday.'

quote: you are not just a scheduler. You represent those guys, so you should really have somebody kinda say, hey. This is what the whole thing looks like.
stewart_read: Customer is essentially coaching the rep on how to carry himself professionally — a sign the rep's passive, filler-heavy delivery undercut his own credibility across the call.
coaching_implication: Rep's repeated 'Yeah. Okay. Yeah.' filler responses read as disengaged; tightening delivery would prevent a customer from having to coach the rep mid-call.
